practice.title: Coffeehouses (≈ 170 palabras)
practice.passage:
In seventeenth-century England, coffeehouses became unusual social spaces. For the price of a penny, a customer could enter, order a cup of coffee, and stay for hours. Because the entry fee was so low, merchants, scholars, and clerks sat side by side, and conversation ranged from business to politics. Contemporaries nicknamed these places "penny universities," suggesting that a visitor could learn as much there as in a classroom.

The coffeehouses also served practical functions. Newspapers and pamphlets were available for customers to read, and shipping news was posted on boards, so merchants could make business decisions quickly. One famous establishment, run by Edward Lloyd, eventually evolved into a center for insuring ships, a development that gave rise to a major financial institution.

Not everyone approved. In 1675, the king attempted to close the coffeehouses, claiming that they encouraged criticism of the government. The ban was withdrawn within days after widespread protest.

items.q: According to the passage, all of the following were available in coffeehouses EXCEPT
items.explain: El texto menciona periódicos, panfletos y noticias de barcos, no libros en venta.

items.q: Why does the author mention the nickname "penny universities"?
options: To show that coffeehouses were cheaper than universities
To suggest that visitors could learn a great deal there
To explain the price of coffee
items.explain: Sugiere que se aprendía tanto como en un aula.

items.q: Why does the author mention Edward Lloyd?
options: To give an example of a coffeehouse that developed into a financial center
items.explain: Ejemplo de evolución a un centro de seguros marítimos.

items.q: Why did the king try to close the coffeehouses?
options: He believed they encouraged criticism of the government
items.explain: «claiming that they encouraged criticism of the government».

items.q: What can be inferred about the 1675 ban?
options: It was quickly reversed because of public opposition

practice.title: Daily Life · Set 1 (correo)
practice.passage:
Subject: Printer credit update

Dear students,

From January 4, each student will receive 150 free pages per semester instead of 200. Color pages count as three black-and-white pages. Unused credit does not carry over. Additional pages can be purchased at the Service Desk (€0.05 per page).

If you believe the system shows an incorrect balance, please send a screenshot to print@unicampus.example by the 15th of the month.

items.q: How many free pages are used by printing 10 color pages?
items.explain: Cada página en color cuenta como 3 en blanco y negro: 30.

practice.title: Daily Life · Set 2 (reglas)
practice.passage:
LIBRARY GROUP ROOMS — BOOKING RULES
• Rooms hold up to six people and may be reserved for a maximum of two hours per day.
• You must check in at the desk within ten minutes of the start time; otherwise the room is released.
• Whiteboards must be cleaned and furniture returned to its original position.
• Groups of two or fewer will be asked to move if others are waiting.

items.q: What happens if a group arrives 15 minutes late?
Why may a group of two be asked to move?
items.explain: «Groups of two or fewer will be asked to move if others are waiting».

items.q: What is the maximum booking time per day?

quiz.q: In an EXCEPT question you should
options: pick the option that appears most
check each option against the text and pick the one NOT there

quiz.q: "Why does the author mention X?" asks you to identify
options: the author's purpose for including X

quiz.q: A rhetorical-purpose answer often starts with a verb like
quiz.explain: to illustrate / to contrast / to support.
